note: Cases needing a disposable VM or a real LAN carry explicit evidence blockers; retired public-remote cases point to rejection tests.

blocked.reason: Needs a disposable Linux VM: the helper's production paths are systemd, NetworkManager and the Docker socket, none of which exist on a macOS workstation. The argv and lifecycle of every one of those paths is unit-tested here; what a VM adds is that the real binaries accept that argv.
blocked.evidence_command: On a DGX Spark or disposable Ubuntu VM: sudo ./packaging/debian/test_install.sh && sudo systemctl status spark-privd.service && cargo test --manifest-path runtime/Cargo.toml -p spark-privd --all-features
blocked.expected_evidence: test_install.sh reports every require_file and account check passing; spark-privd.service is active with Group=sparkd; the socket is root:sparkd 0660.

blocked.reason: Needs a second machine on an isolated LAN. The TXT record contract and the parsing on both sides are unit-tested; what a LAN adds is that mDNS actually propagates between two hosts.
blocked.evidence_command: With a Spark and a Mac on one isolated switch: dns-sd -B _spark-runtime._tcp local. and then dns-sd -L <instance> _spark-runtime._tcp local.
blocked.expected_evidence: The browse lists the node instance; the lookup prints the TXT keys with a tls_fingerprint matching GET /api/v1/identity on that node.
